scope_note: Twelve trades, US practice, hand-curated. Chosen so that all seven constraint types are exercised and every name is one an EPC judge recognises. Depth beats breadth.
advisory_notice: Every row is advisory and contractual. WORKFACE plans the work and produces the record; it does not certify, and it does not replace the field measurement (surface thermometer, sling psychrometer, base-material probe) that the referenced standards require an inspector to perform.

verify_status_legend.primary: Threshold read from the manufacturer's own PDS/TDS, the standards body's own published text, or a government publication. A human can open source_url and see the number.
verify_status_legend.secondary: Threshold quoted by a reputable industry body / DOT / trade association that cites the paywalled standard. The number is trustworthy; the clause wording is not verbatim from the standard itself.
verify_status_legend.partial: Some values in the row are primary and some are interpolated or project-specific. See verify_note. DO NOT use in the field without replacing with the project's approved values.

cost_note: unit_cost_usd and rework_multiplier are indicative US 2026 trade pricing ranges used to drive the $ at-risk / $ protected counters. They are NOT cited standards. Rework multipliers are shaped by CII field-rework benchmark research (direct field rework ~5% of construction value, 90th percentile 12.4%). Show this note in the counter tooltip.

constraints.label: Concrete temperature at discharge ≤ 35 °C (95 °F)
constraints.citation_fragment: ACI 301-20 'Specifications for Concrete Construction' and ACI 305.1-14 'Specification for Hot Weather Concreting' limit the maximum concrete temperature to 95 °F (35 °C) at the time of discharge.

units.V: wind velocity, mph (average of steady wind and gust)

constraints.label: ACI 305 evaporation rate ≤ 0.2 lb/ft²/hr
constraints.citation_fragment: Precautions against plastic shrinkage cracking are required when the calculated evaporation rate reaches 0.2 lb/ft²/hr (1.0 kg/m²/h) for conventional concrete, and 0.1 lb/ft²/hr (0.5 kg/m²/h) for low-bleed mixes such as Type 1L blended cements. FHWA states that at ≥ 1.0 kg/m²/h 'definite action to retard evaporation is necessary'. NJDOT MP 29-08 requires placement to be discontinued when the evaporation rate reaches or exceeds 0.15 lb/ft²/hr.

trades.citation: ACI 301-20 §4 and ACI 305.1-14 §3.2–3.3 limit maximum concrete temperature to 95 °F (35 °C) at time of discharge; a higher temperature is permitted only with successful past field experience or preconstruction testing and prior approval of the architect/engineer. ACI 305R plastic-shrinkage guidance sets an evaporation-rate precaution threshold of 0.2 lb/ft²/hr (0.1 lb/ft²/hr for low-bleed mixes). ACI 305R defines hot weather as 'any combination of high air temperature, low relative humidity, wind speed, and solar radiation' — not a temperature.
trades.verify_note: 95 °F/35 °C confirmed verbatim on ACI's own FAQ page, which names ACI 301-20 and ACI 305.1-14 and (via NIH ORF bulletin) sections 3.2 and 3.3. Evaporation thresholds confirmed against FHWA (1.0 and 0.5 kg/m²/h = 0.205 and 0.102 lb/ft²/hr). The exact ACI 305R figure number for the nomograph is NOT verified — do not cite a figure number on a slide.

constraints.direction_note: This is a TRIGGER, not a prohibition. Below it, cold-weather protection procedures become mandatory.
constraints.label: Cold-weather procedures triggered below 4 °C (40 °F) air
constraints.citation_fragment: ACI 306R-16 §1.1: the conditions of cold weather concreting exist 'when the air temperature has fallen to, or is expected to fall below, 40 °F (4 °C) during the protection period'.

constraints.label: Protection period: ≥ 72 h continuous run above the protection temperature
constraints.citation_fragment: ACI 306R-16 §2.2 defines the protection period as 'the time recommended to prevent concrete from being adversely affected by exposure to cold weather during construction'. The duration and the protection temperature are project-specific and set by the engineer of record.

trades.citation: ACI 306R-16 §1.1: cold weather concreting conditions exist 'when the air temperature has fallen to, or is expected to fall below, 40 °F (4 °C) during the protection period.' §2.2 defines the protection period as 'the time recommended to prevent concrete from being adversely affected by exposure to cold weather during construction.'
trades.standard_ref: ACI 306R-16 §1.1, §2.2 (protection temperatures: Table 5.1; protection duration: Ch. 7)
trades.verify_note: The 40 °F (4 °C) definition is PRIMARY — quoted verbatim from ACI's own published preview of 306R-16 and independently from an NIH technical bulletin. The 72 h protection duration and the 10 °C protection temperature are NOT from ACI Table 5.1 (paywalled and not obtained). They are demo placeholders that stand in for a project-specific value the EOR sets. Replace before any field use, and say so if a judge asks. This row exists mainly to carry the January `direction: below` slide.

constraints.label: Air 1.7–48.9 °C (35–120 °F)
constraints.citation_fragment: Macropoxy 646 PDS, Application Conditions — Air: 35 °F (1.7 °C) minimum, 120 °F (49 °C) maximum.

constraints.label: Surface 1.7–121.1 °C (35–250 °F)
constraints.citation_fragment: Macropoxy 646 PDS, Application Conditions — Surface: 35 °F (1.7 °C) minimum, 250 °F (120 °C) maximum. Material: 40 °F (4.5 °C) minimum.

constraints.label: Surface ≥ dew point + 2.8 °C (5 °F)
constraints.citation_fragment: SSPC-PA 1 §6.2: 'Coating shall not be applied … when the steel surface temperature is less than 5 °F (3 °C) above the dew point.' Macropoxy 646 PDS: 'At least 5 °F (2.8 °C) above dew point.'

constraints.label: Relative humidity ≤ 85 %
constraints.citation_fragment: Macropoxy 646 PDS, Application Conditions — Relative humidity: 85 % maximum. SSPC-PA 1 §6.3: 'no coating shall be applied unless the manufacturer's written requirements for humidity are met.'

constraints.label: Cure to service — temperature-dependent integral
constraints.citation_fragment: Macropoxy 646 PDS drying schedule at 7.0 mils wet: cure to service (atmospheric) 10 days @ 35 °F, 7 days @ 77 °F, 4 days @ 100 °F. Recoat minimum 48 h / 8 h / 4.5 h at the same three temperatures; recoat maximum 1 year.

trades.citation: Sherwin-Williams Macropoxy 646 Fast Cure Epoxy PDS (rev. 21 May 2020), Application Conditions: air 35–120 °F, surface 35–250 °F, material minimum 40 °F, at least 5 °F (2.8 °C) above dew point, relative humidity 85 % maximum. Drying schedule at 7.0 mils wet: cure to service (atmospheric) 10 days @ 35 °F, 7 days @ 77 °F, 4 days @ 100 °F. SSPC-PA 1 §6.2: coating shall not be applied when the steel surface temperature is less than 5 °F (3 °C) above the dew point.
trades.standard_ref: SSPC-PA 1 (AMPP) §6.1–6.3 — Shop, Field and Maintenance Coating of Metals; Sherwin-Williams Macropoxy 646 PDS
trades.verify_note: Every number read directly off the Macropoxy 646 PDS. SSPC-PA 1 §6.2 wording read off a published copy of the specification. This is the hero row — the demo drawer quotes it inline. The three cure-table points are the calibration set for the Q10 fit; plot the fit against them in the app (test_cure.py, Day 4).

constraints.label: Substrate and ambient ≥ 4 °C (40 °F), maintained ≥ 24 h after application
constraints.citation_fragment: CAFCO 300 TDS §1.7.1: 'When the prevailing outdoor temperature at the building is less than 40 °F (4 °C), a minimum substrate and ambient temperature of 40 °F (4 °C) shall be maintained prior to, during, and a minimum of 24 hours after application.'

constraints.label: ≥ 4 air changes/hour until dry (site condition, not a temperature)
constraints.citation_fragment: CAFCO 300 TDS §1.7.2.1: 'Ventilation must not be less than 4 complete air exchanges per hour until the material is dry.'

trades.citation: Isolatek CAFCO 300 / ISOLATEK Type 300 Technical Data Sheet (C-TDS 05/20) §1.7.1: 'When the prevailing outdoor temperature at the building is less than 40 °F (4 °C), a minimum substrate and ambient temperature of 40 °F (4 °C) shall be maintained prior to, during, and a minimum of 24 hours after application.' §1.7.2.1: 'Ventilation must not be less than 4 complete air exchanges per hour until the material is dry.'
trades.standard_ref: Isolatek CAFCO 300 TDS §1.7 (C-TDS 05/20); UL Evaluation Report UL ER13348-01
trades.verify_note: Read verbatim from Isolatek's own TDS. This is the pure `continuity` row and it is exactly what FortyGuard's `persistence` analytic computes — pre-screen tiles with one API call before running the local evaluation. Say that out loud.

trades.display_name: Adhesive anchors — injection epoxy into concrete

constraints.label: Base material −5 to +40 °C (23–104 °F) at installation
constraints.citation_fragment: Hilti HIT-RE 500 V3 technical data: installation (base material) temperature range −5 °C to +40 °C (23 °F to 104 °F).

constraints.label: Working time collapses from 120 min at 0 °C to 10 min at 40 °C
constraints.citation_fragment: Hilti HIT-RE 500 V3 technical data, working time and curing time vs base material temperature. Curing times double in wet base material conditions.

trades.citation: Hilti HIT-RE 500 V3 Injection Mortar technical datasheet (updated Aug-19): installation (base material) temperature range −5 °C to +40 °C (23 °F to 104 °F). Working time / minimum curing time by base material temperature: −5 to −1 °C → 120 min / 168 h; 0–4 °C → 120 min / 48 h; 5–9 °C → 120 min / 24 h; 10–14 °C → 90 min / 16 h; 15–19 °C → 60 min / 12 h; 20–24 °C → 30 min / 7 h; 25–29 °C → 20 min / 6 h; 30–34 °C → 15 min / 5 h; 35–39 °C → 12 min / 4.5 h; 40 °C → 10 min / 4 h. Curing times double in wet base material.
trades.standard_ref: Hilti HIT-RE 500 V3 IFU / technical data (ICC-ES ESR-3814 governs the qualification)
trades.verify_note: Full table read off Hilti's own datasheet. Note the direction: in Phoenix August the binding number is not the 104 °F ceiling, it is the 10-minute working time — the crew physically cannot place the anchors before the mortar gels. That is a far more interesting demo beat than 'too hot'.

constraints.label: Air ≥ 4.4 °C (40 °F) and rising
constraints.citation_fragment: TxDOT (as quoted in Research Report 214-11): 'The prime coat, tack coat or the asphaltic mixtures … shall not be placed when the air temperature is below 50 °F and falling; but it may be placed when the air temperature is above 40 °F and rising.'

constraints.label: Available compaction minutes = f(base surface temperature, lift thickness)
constraints.citation_fragment: Available compaction time is a function of base surface temperature and mat thickness. TxDOT Research Report 214-11 Tables 2–4: for base temperatures 20–50 °F with air 10–40 °F, a 3 in mat gives 26–34 min, a 2 in mat 16–21.5 min and a 1 in mat 5–7 min. For base above 90 °F, the window runs from about 4 min at a 13 mm lift to about 15 min at a 50 mm lift.

trades.citation: TxDOT Research Report 214-11 (Environmental Conditions for Placing Asphalt Concrete), Tables 2–4: available compaction time in minutes as a function of base surface temperature and mat thickness — base 20–50 °F with air 10–40 °F gives 26–34 min for a 3 in mat, 16–21.5 min for a 2 in mat and 5–7 min for a 1 in mat. The report's central finding is that an air-temperature-only cessation rule 'prohibits the placement of asphalt concrete several days a year in the southern part of the state' for thick lifts while being 'not sufficiently restrictive for thin lifts'.
trades.standard_ref: TxDOT Research Report 214-11; Asphalt Institute MS-22 cessation practice; project specification governs
trades.verify_note: The cold-base rows (Tables 2–4 of TxDOT 214-11) and the hot-base row (>32 °C) are read from published sources. The INTERMEDIATE base-temperature rows are linearly interpolated by us and are NOT published values. Replace with the project's approved cessation table before any field use. This row is the cheapest proof that WORKFACE is not a heat alarm: hot weather HELPS asphalt compaction and hurts everything else, on the same tile in the same hour.

constraints.label: Hot-weather procedures triggered above 37.8 °C (100 °F)
constraints.citation_fragment: TMS 602 hot weather requirements are triggered 'above 100 °F (37.8 °C) or above 90 °F (32.2 °C) with a wind speed greater than 8 mph'.

constraints.expression: trigger_tier1 iff (Ta_F > 100) or (Ta_F > 90 and V_mph > 8); trigger_tier2 iff (Ta_F > 115) or (Ta_F > 105 and V_mph > 8)
constraints.label: Wind-modified hot-weather trigger (this is why wind matters, not just heat)
constraints.citation_fragment: Tier 1 — above 100 °F, or above 90 °F with wind > 8 mph: maintain sand piles damp and loose, keep mortar and grout below 120 °F, use mortar within 2 hours of initial mixing, fog spray newly constructed masonry until damp at least three times a day until the masonry is three days old. Tier 2 — above 115 °F, or above 105 °F with wind > 8 mph: additionally shade materials and mixing equipment from direct sunlight and use cool mixing water; ice is permitted provided it is melted when added.

trades.citation: TMS 602 / ACI 530.1 hot weather construction requirements as summarised in Brick Industry Association Technical Note 1, Tables 2a/2b: preparation and construction procedures are triggered above 100 °F (37.8 °C) or above 90 °F (32.2 °C) with a wind speed greater than 8 mph — 'maintain sand piles in a damp, loose condition; maintain temperature of mortar and grout below 120 °F; use mortar within 2 hours of initial mixing'; protection requires 'fog spray all newly constructed masonry until damp, at least three times a day until the masonry is three days old'. A second tier applies above 115 °F (46.1 °C) or above 105 °F (40.6 °C) with wind greater than 8 mph.
trades.standard_ref: TMS 602 / ACI 530.1 / ASCE 6 Article 1.8 C — Hot Weather Construction (via BIA Technical Note 1)
trades.verify_note: Numbers and wording quoted from an industry technical note that reproduces the TMS 602 hot/cold weather tables. TMS 602 itself is paywalled. The thresholds are consistent across BIA TN 1 and CMHA TEK 03-01C. Cite the Technical Note on the slide, not the standard's article number, unless someone on the team buys TMS 602 and checks it.

constraints.label: Do not lay masonry units having a temperature below −6.7 °C (20 °F)
constraints.citation_fragment: TMS 602 cold weather construction: 'Do not lay masonry units having a temperature below 20 °F.'

constraints.label: Maintain masonry above 0 °C (32 °F) for 24 h (48 h if grouted)
constraints.citation_fragment: Below 20 °F (−6.7 °C): 'Maintain masonry temperature above 32 °F (0 °C) for 24 hours … by enclosure with supplementary heat' — 48 hours for grouted masonry unless Type III cement is used. At 25–32 °F: insulating blanket coverage for 24 hours (48 hours for grouted masonry). At 32–40 °F: 'Protect completed masonry from rain or snow by covering with a weather-resistive membrane for 24 hours after construction.'

trades.citation: TMS 602 / ACI 530.1 cold weather construction requirements as summarised in Brick Industry Association Technical Note 1, Tables 1a/1b: at 32–40 °F, 'protect completed masonry from rain or snow by covering with a weather-resistive membrane for 24 hours after construction'; at 25–32 °F, 'do not lay masonry units having a temperature below 20 °F' and provide insulating blanket coverage for 24 hours (48 hours for grouted masonry); below 20 °F, 'maintain masonry temperature above 32 °F (0 °C) for 24 hours … by enclosure with supplementary heat' (48 hours for grouted masonry unless Type III cement is used).
trades.standard_ref: TMS 602 / ACI 530.1 / ASCE 6 Article 1.8 C — Cold Weather Construction (via BIA Technical Note 1)
trades.verify_note: Same source and same caveat as the hot-weather masonry row. Note this row governs on BASE MATERIAL temperature (the temperature of the unit itself), not air — a CMU stacked on a pallet in the sun and a CMU in shade are different units to this rule. That is a WORKFACE point, not a weather-app point.

constraints.label: Substrate −29 to +50 °C (−20 to +122 °F) during installation
constraints.citation_fragment: DOWSIL 795 TDS: do not apply 'when surface temperatures exceed 50 °C (122 °F) during installation'. Dow cold-weather installation guide: minimum application temperature −20 °F (−29 °C) for DOWSIL 790/791/795/995/756/758.

constraints.label: Substrate above dew point, clean, dry and frost-free
constraints.citation_fragment: Dow cold-weather installation guide: 'When caulking at temperatures below the dew and frost point, 40 °F / 4 °C and lower, the surfaces must be clean, dry and frost-free.' DOWSIL 795 TDS: do not apply 'on frost laden or wet surfaces'. 'A moisture meter should be used to ensure the substrates are dry before caulking.'

trades.citation: DOWSIL 795 Silicone Building Sealant TDS (Form No. 61-885-01 S, 2017): do not apply 'on frost laden or wet surfaces' or 'when surface temperatures exceed 50 °C (122 °F) during installation'; tack-free 3 h and full cure 7–14 days at 25 °C / 50 % RH. Dow 'Installation of DOWSIL Silicone Building Sealants in Cold Weather': minimum application temperature −20 °F (−29 °C); 'when caulking at temperatures below the dew and frost point, 40 °F / 4 °C and lower, the surfaces must be clean, dry and frost-free'; 'a moisture meter should be used to ensure the substrates are dry before caulking'. ASTM C1193 is the governing guide for joint sealant use.
trades.standard_ref: ASTM C1193 — Standard Guide for Use of Joint Sealants; DOWSIL 795 TDS Form 61-885-01 S
trades.verify_note: Temperature limits and the dry/frost-free rule are read off Dow's own TDS and cold-weather guide. The delta_c of 0.0 on the dew-point offset is deliberate: unlike SSPC-PA 1, Dow specifies 'dry and frost-free', not a numeric offset. Do NOT invent a 5 °F offset here — the honest model is 'substrate at or above dew point and verified dry'. ASTM C1193 itself is paywalled and was not read.

constraints.label: Pavement and air ≥ 12.8 °C (55 °F) and rising; never below 7.2 °C (45 °F)
constraints.citation_fragment: Sherwin-Williams Sher-Flight Waterborne Traffic Paint: minimum air and surface temperature 55 °F and rising; extended drying and reduced service life between 45 °F and 55 °F; do not apply below 45 °F. MoDOT EPG 620.11: 50 °F is the recommended minimum application temperature on minor roads and 60 °F on major roads; below that, film durability drops to '2 to 3 months instead of 9 to 12 months'.

constraints.label: Pavement dry and above dew point (waterborne film must release water)
constraints.citation_fragment: Waterborne paint dries by evaporation of water; MoDOT notes 'dry times are dependent on temperature and humidity' and that 'low temperature and high humidity result in longer dry times'. A pavement at or below dew point will not release the film's water and the line will track.

trades.citation: Sherwin-Williams Sher-Flight Waterborne Traffic Paint technical bulletin (06/18): minimum air and surface temperature 55 °F and rising; extended drying and reduced service life between 45 °F and 55 °F; do not apply below 45 °F; a uniform line at 14–16 mils wet 'should dry in 10 minutes or less'. MoDOT Engineering Policy Guide 620.11: '50 °Fahrenheit is the recommended minimum application temperature' on minor roads, 60 °F on major roads; a cold-weather formulation may be applied at 'air and surface temperatures of 35° (and climbing)'.
trades.standard_ref: Sherwin-Williams Sher-Flight PDS; MoDOT EPG 620.11; project DOT specification governs
trades.verify_note: The 55 °F-and-rising and 45 °F floor are PRIMARY (Sherwin-Williams' own bulletin). The MoDOT 50/60 °F figures are PRIMARY from MoDOT's policy guide. The 1.7 °C dew-point offset on `offset_surface_dry` is OURS, not a published number — no source we found specifies a numeric dew-point offset for waterborne marking. Either drop the numeric offset and treat it as a binary 'pavement dry' condition, or find a state DOT spec that gives one. Do not put the 1.7 °C on a slide.

constraints.label: Minimum preheat/interpass by thickness — a preheat trigger, not a hard stop
constraints.citation_fragment: AWS D1.1 prequalified minimum preheat and interpass temperature, Category B steels (A36, A572 Gr 42/50, A992 shapes, A709 Gr 36/50/50W) with SMAW low-hydrogen, FCAW, GMAW or SAW: 1/8 to 3/4 in → 32 °F; over 3/4 to 1-1/2 in → 50 °F; over 1-1/2 to 2-1/2 in → 150 °F; over 2-1/2 in → 225 °F.

trades.citation: AWS D1.1 Structural Welding Code — Steel, prequalified minimum preheat and interpass temperature table, Category B (shapes and plates including A36, A529 Gr 42, A709 Gr 36/50/50W, A572 Gr 42 and 50, A992 Gr 50 shapes) with SMAW using low-hydrogen electrodes, or FCAW, GMAW or SAW: thickest part at the point of welding 3–19 mm (1/8–3/4 in) → 32 °F; over 19 to 38.1 mm (3/4–1-1/2 in) → 50 °F; over 38.1 to 63.5 mm (1-1/2–2-1/2 in) → 150 °F; over 63.5 mm (over 2-1/2 in) → 225 °F.
trades.standard_ref: AWS D1.1/D1.1M Structural Welding Code — Steel, prequalified preheat table (Table 3.2 in older editions, Table 5.8 in D1.1:2020); reproduced in UFC 3-320-01A Table 3-1
trades.verify_note: Values read from UFC 3-320-01A Table 3-1, a US government publication that reproduces the AWS D1.1 prequalified table. AWS D1.1 itself is paywalled and was not read. The table NUMBER differs by edition — say 'the AWS D1.1 prequalified preheat table', not 'Table 3.2', on any slide. This row is deliberately modelled as a MITIGATION trigger rather than a hard stop: cold steel does not stop welding, it obliges preheat, which costs crew-hours and fuel. That nuance is a good demo beat.

trades.display_name: Crew heat exposure — WBGT work/rest and OSHA triggers

constraints.label: OSHA proposed initial heat trigger — heat index 80 °F
constraints.citation_fragment: OSHA proposed Heat Injury and Illness Prevention rule, initial heat trigger: 'a heat index of 80 °F or a wet bulb globe temperature equal to the NIOSH Recommended Action Limit'. Requires cool drinking water, break areas with cooling measures, acclimatisation protocols for new and returning unacclimatised employees, paid rest breaks if needed to prevent overheating, and regular and effective two-way communication.

constraints.label: OSHA proposed high heat trigger — heat index 90 °F, 15 min break every 2 h
constraints.citation_fragment: OSHA proposed high heat trigger: 'heat index of 90 °F or wet bulb globe temperature equal to the NIOSH Recommended Exposure Limit'. Requires 'mandatory rest breaks of 15 minutes at least every two hours', observation for signs and symptoms of heat-related illness, and a hazard alert.

constraints.label: WBGT → work/rest ratio → productive crew hours
constraints.citation_fragment: OSHA Technical Manual Section III Chapter 4 gives the outdoor WBGT equation WBGT_out = 0.7*T_nwb + 0.2*T_globe + 0.1*T_db. The ACGIH TLV screening criteria that map WBGT to a work/rest allocation are copyrighted by ACGIH and are NOT reproduced here; the bands used by WORKFACE are our own placeholders pending a licensed copy.

trades.citation: OSHA proposed Heat Injury and Illness Prevention standard (NPRM published 30 August 2024): initial heat trigger is 'a heat index of 80 °F or a wet bulb globe temperature equal to the NIOSH Recommended Action Limit'; high heat trigger is 'heat index of 90 °F or wet bulb globe temperature equal to the NIOSH Recommended Exposure Limit', which requires 'mandatory rest breaks of 15 minutes at least every two hours'. The rule is NOT final — the informal public hearing closed 2 July 2025 and the post-hearing comment period closed 30 October 2025, with no target date announced for a final rule as of mid-2026. In the interim OSHA enforces heat under the General Duty Clause, Section 5(a)(1), and renewed its Heat National Emphasis Program on 10 April 2026 for five further years through 2031. The outdoor WBGT equation is WBGT = 0.7*T_nwb + 0.2*T_globe + 0.1*T_air (OSHA Technical Manual III:4).
trades.standard_ref: OSHA Heat Injury and Illness Prevention NPRM (89 FR, 30 Aug 2024); OSHA Technical Manual Section III Ch. 4; ACGIH TLV Heat Stress and Strain (7th ed. documentation, licensed — not reproduced); Liljegren et al. (2008) WBGT model
trades.verify_note: The 80 °F / 90 °F triggers and the 15-min-every-2-h break are PRIMARY, quoted from OSHA's own rulemaking fact sheet. The rulemaking STATUS (stalled, NEP renewed 10 Apr 2026 through 2031) is verified and is worth saying on stage — it shows you checked rather than assumed. The WBGT→work/rest BANDS ARE OURS. OSHA's own Technical Manual states the ACGIH screening table 'is copyrighted by ACGIH and is not publicly available'. Label the bands in the UI as 'WORKFACE placeholder bands, pending ACGIH licence' — do not present them as the ACGIH TLV. This is the single most likely place for a judge to catch us.
